# UI renderers

How a UI plugin's interface reaches a host that is not Datalayer's own page, one spec each
under `agentspecs/ui-renderers/`. A renderer is not an interface: a [UI plugin](./index.mdx)
says the renderers it may be exposed through, and an application names, per UI plugin, the
one it uses. A renderer that is not enabled is listed, and an application that is offered
cannot use it yet.

| Renderer | Id | Enabled | The UI plugins it can carry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [A2UI](https://a2ui.org/) | `a2ui` | yes | `a2ui-surface`, `a2ui-view`, `app-components`, `app-elements`, `app-page` |
| [MCP Apps](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/extensions/apps) | `mcp-apps` | no | `app-page` |
| [MCP UI](https://mcpui.dev/) | `mcp-ui` | no | `pap-sign-in` |

## Each renderer

### A2UI (`a2ui`)

An agent describes an interface — a form, a table, a card — as a tree of components from a catalogue the host allows, and the host renders it; what the user does in it comes back to the agent as an action.

### MCP Apps (`mcp-apps`)

An MCP server ships an interactive app with a tool: the host renders it in a sandboxed frame beside the conversation, and the app calls the server's tools through the host.

### MCP UI (`mcp-ui`)

An MCP tool answers with a UI resource — HTML, a remote page or a component — that the host renders in place of plain text.
